newsitem.title: DUBAI: OPEC ministers to address Iran oil conference in May.
newsitem.headline: OPEC ministers to address Iran oil conference in May.

text.p: OPEC ministers from Iran, Kuwait, Nigeria and Qatar will address a conference on the future of the Middle East oil and gas industry in Isfahan, Iran from May 8-10, organisers National Iranian Oil Corp said.
OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman also will address the three-day conference, the organisers said.

Senior managers are also expected from France's Total SA, Malaysian national oil firm Petronas, Australian BHP Petroleum, China National Petroleum Corp, Royal Dutch Shell, British Gas, Gaz de France, Elf Aquitaine and Italy's Ente Nazionale Idrocarburi (ENI).

The conference will start on May 8 with a ministerial session including speeches from the four OPEC ministers, the Turkish minister of energy Recai Kutan and the president of the World Petroleum Congresses (WPC).

Sessions for May 9, organisers said, have been selected as: Global energy fundamentals - implications for the Middle East; Geopolitics of energy - dynamics and challenges; Asia and the Middle East - growing strategic partnerships; and Middle East and the global gas agenda.

Sessions on May 10 are: International petroleum investments - realities and constraints; The world oil market - imperatives of policy interventions; Oil trade and marketing - competing forces; Middle East in transition - continuity or change.

Iranian officials speaking at Isfahan include oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh, director of international affairs at the National Iranian Oil Company Hojatollah Ghanimifard, deputy minister for international affairs at Ministry of Petroleum M. Nejadhosseinian, and deputy minister and managing director National Iranian Gas Company Mohammad-Nejad.

Iran last hosted an energy conference in Isfahan in 1991 when it announced a policy of allowing foreign investment in its vital oil and gas sector for the first time since its 1979 Islamic revolution.
Total and Petronas are so far the only firms with direct energy investment in Iran with the Sirri E and A offshore oil and gas field development.
Iran has the fourth largest reserves of oil in the world and the second biggest gas deposits after Russia.
